Each bill would have created a detailed scheme: written parental request to the principal (with patient card, physician certification, necessity statement, and caregiver authorisation); a principal-designated isolated administration area; transport and locked storage by the caregiver or a county-designated caregiver (a county health department employee designated by the Department, registered as a caregiver); a ban on obstructing a qualified student's access during the school day; funding from the Department of Health Grants and Donations Trust Fund (from §381.986 fees); and Department rulemaking — plus an amendment to §1006.062(8) and a §381.986(14) exception allowing school personnel to possess a student's medical marijuana pursuant to the §1006.062(8) policies. None of that is law. The bills:

Bill Session Outcome (official bill page)
SB 986 2018 Indefinitely postponed and withdrawn from consideration, 10 Mar 2018; died in Health Policy
HB 1291 2018 Indefinitely postponed and withdrawn from consideration, 10 Mar 2018; died in Health Quality Subcommittee
SB 384 2019 Died in Health Policy, 3 May 2019 (indefinitely postponed and withdrawn from consideration) — https://flhouse.gov/Sections/Bills/billsdetail.aspx?BillId=63252 — Accessed 2026-10-24
SB 720 2020 Died in Health Policy, 14 Mar 2020 (indefinitely postponed and withdrawn from consideration)

Sources: TrackBill histories for SB 986 (2018), HB 1291 (2018), SB 384 (2019), SB 720 (2020) — https://trackbill.com/bill/florida-senate-bill-986-medical-use-of-marijuana-in-schools/1492765/, https://trackbill.com/bill/florida-house-bill-1291-medical-use-of-marijuana-in-schools/1509704/, https://trackbill.com/bill/florida-senate-bill-384-medical-use-of-marijuana-in-schools/1641319/, https://trackbill.com/bill/florida-senate-bill-720-medical-use-of-marijuana-in-schools/1772883/ — Accessed 2026-10-24 (secondary trackers; bill texts on flsenate.gov: SB 986 (2018) — https://flsenate.gov/Session/Bill/2018/986/BillText/Filed/PDF; SB 384 (2019) — https://flsenate.gov/Session/Bill/2019/384/BillText/Filed/HTML; SB 720 (2020) — https://FLSenate.gov/Session/Bill/2020/720/BillText/Filed/PDF — Accessed 2026-10-24). Consequences of the deaths: there is no statutory "county-designated caregiver," no statutory isolated-area requirement, no statutory non-obstruction rule, and no statutory school-personnel possession exception in §381.986(14) for schools — only the §1006.062(8) district-policy mandate. Any source describing the county-designated-caregiver scheme as current law is describing a dead bill. (Note: the 2018 bill texts also contain a §381.986(14) paragraph allowing school personnel to possess a student's marijuana "pursuant to policies and procedures established pursuant to s. 1006.62(8)" — that paragraph was part of the proposed amendment, not the enacted §381.986(14); CORRECTED in Audit: the enacted §381.986(14)(h) DOES contain school-personnel possession language, pursuant to policies under §1006.062(8) — see Audit correction, Part 12. Gap 12-12 is resolved on this point.)

12.9.4 Schools, hemp, and non-patients — the boundaries

  • Non-patient students: possession/use of marijuana on school grounds by a non-patient student is a Chapter 893 offence (and a student-discipline matter under §1006.07/§1006.13 zero-tolerance policies) with no §1006.062(8) protection — §1006.062(8) protects only "a student who is a qualified patient."
  • Hemp products at school: §1006.062(8) is about marijuana obtained under §381.986. It does not authorise hemp extract use at school, and it does not prohibit it either. A hemp product that is lawful under §581.217 (≤0.3% total delta-9, 21+ for ingestion/inhalation — a rule aimed at sellers, not at school possession) is not marijuana, so it is not within §381.986(12)(c) — but a school's own drug/controlled-substance discipline policy, and any local rule, may still prohibit it on campus, and a product that tests over-limit is marijuana, not hemp. No school-specific hemp rule was located [UNAVAILABLE].
  • Postsecondary institutions: §1006.062 covers district school boards (K-12). Colleges and universities are not within §1006.062(8); their marijuana policies are institutional (and, for federally funded institutions, federal Drug-Free Schools and Communities Act policies), not §1006.062 policies. No Florida statute requiring a college to permit medical marijuana use on campus was located [UNAVAILABLE].

C. Conflicts log (both runs — how each was handled)

  • OMMU patient/location figures by week are successive snapshots, not conflicts — latest dated snapshot wins, earlier snapshots retained with dates.
  • Amendment 3 totals: election-night pair (Run 1) replaced by certified pair (Run 2); percentage unchanged at 55.90%.
  • Total MMTC licences (27 vs 28 vs 49 vs 50): NOT resolved — no single total asserted anywhere in either run.
  • Dollar sales (Headset vs Brightfield vs BDSA vs MJBizDaily): NOT resolved — no official series settles it; no figure adopted as official.
  • CMTL count (9 vs 8 vs 6) and fee ($78,000 vs [REMOVED as a current fee — Audit confirms $78,000; see Audit table]): NOT resolved — different years/bases, no official directory located.
  • Physician counts (2,462 vs 2,247, plus 2,458–2,466 in Nov 2025): NOT resolved, reason for movement unexplained in sources.
  • Verde banking scope (Florida Trend vs USF's own page): NOT resolved — do not quote plant-touching claim as current without re-confirming with USF.
  • FDACS seizure cumulative totals (631,000/420,000 vs 1.3 million): treated as successive cumulative totals, latest wins, definitions differing.
  • §381.986 Schedule I consent language vs fixed Schedule III baseline: flagged, not resolved by picking one — Florida text has not caught up.
  • Secondary “combined 24,500 mg” 70-day figure vs per-route rule table: resolved in favour of the rule table; cross-route aggregate question left open.
  • “Combined” hemp acreage (approved vs planted): approved/permitted acreage is not production — planted acres (29 in 2025) are the production measure.
  • Seminole County moratorium (Run 1 Part 3) vs Seminole Tribe: clarified in Run 2 Part 10 — the moratorium is the county, not the tribe.
  • 5 ng/mL THC driving figure (one secondary source): REJECTED — that is a Colorado/Washington limit, not Florida's; Florida is impairment-based with no per se THC limit.
  • HB 1597 hemp festival/school-buffer claims (secondary): NOT adopted — HB 1409/SB 1270 (2026) festival-sale bans died 13 Mar 2026 and are not law.
